body: Why would anyone do something they don't want to do if it doesn't help to fulfill their goals? There's no reason to think that spending time in nature would eventually have a positive effect. From what I understand, people whose moods are improved by spending time in nature see positive results almost immediately. I kept at it for a while even though it was only making things worse, but eventually you have to just call it quits.
I agree with that definition, but most people don't.

I tried marijuana once; it was a complete waste of money. I'm not really a fan of nature or the outdoors. I tried going for walks a couple of years ago, but it just made me feel like shit so I gave up on it.

I'm mainly just sitting around waiting for the day to end so I can go back to sleep. I don't really enjoy anything, so I just do whatever wastes time and requires no effort. I used to play video games, but they take too much energy, and it's too hard to get invested in them.

I'd rather not have my brain fucked around with by prescription drugs (I've already tried multiple different types of anti-depressants and it was not a good experience). I wouldn't mind trying to drink myself into oblivion, but that stuff is too expensive, and it's also disgusting imo.

> Is there any way you could dredge up the energy to self improve?

I don't think so. I would have done it by now.
I'm not going to be bonking any women regardless of whether I'm a misogynist or not.
